'''Habib Ibrahim Rahimtoola''' (10 March 1912 – 2 January 1991) was a Pakistani politician, and diplomat primarily based in Karachi.<ref>{{cite web|title=Pakistani politician, industrialist, trader, diplomat|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=8NQ_AAAAMAAJ&q=habib+rahimtoola+diplomat|website=Google Books|year = 2000}}</ref> He served as Pakistan's High Commissioner to the United Kingdom (1947–52).<ref name="urlHabib Ibrahim Rahimtoola [& Wife] - LIFE">{{cite magazine |url=http://www.life.com/image/50774540 |title=Habib Ibrahim Rahimtoola [& Wife] - LIFE |magazine=LIFE |format= |accessdate=2009-06-08}}</ref> Rahimtoola also served as [[Governor of Sindh]] (1953–54) and later as the [[Governor of Punjab (Pakistan)|Governor of Punjab]] (1954).<ref>{{cite web|title=Governors of Sind|url=http://www.governorsindh.gov.pk/governors/|website=Sindh Governor Official site|accessdate=22 August 2016|archive-date=4 July 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160704001823/http://www.governorsindh.gov.pk/governors/|url-status=dead}}</ref> He is considered one of the [[List of Pakistan Movement activists|founders of Pakistan]] for his involvement as a leader of the [[Pakistan Movement]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Pakistani politician, industrialist, trader, diplomat|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=8NQ_AAAAMAAJ&q=habib+rahimtoola+diplomat|website=Google Books|year = 2000}}</ref>

==Early life and political career==
[[File:Habib I. Rahimtoola, Begum Rahimtoola, Brigadier Ghawas, and General SMA Faruki.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Left to right: Habib with his wife [[Zubeida Rahimtoola]], Brigadier [[Syed Ghawas]], and General SMA Faruki at the Pakistan House in [[London]] (1951)]]
Rahimtoola was initially educated at [[St. Xavier's Collegiate School|St. Xavier's School]], [[Calcutta]], where he also received his [[Bachelor of Arts]] at the affiliated [[St. Xavier's College, Kolkata]], both being in the top tier of educational institutions in Calcutta. He then received an [[LL.B]] 1935.<ref>{{cite web|title=Tehreek-e-Pakistan Key Mujahid|url=http://www.pakpost.gov.pk/philately/stamps2002/independence_day.html|website=[[Pakistan Post]]|accessdate=22 August 2016}}</ref>

He entered politics at an early age and became Secretary General of the Muslim Students Union at his college between 1927 and 1931. After completing his further education Rahimtoola proceeded to business affairs. He was also  a supporter of the [[All-India Muslim League|Muslim League]]. He founded and was the first president of the Bombay Provincial [[Bombay Legislative Council|Muslim Chamber of Commerce]] (1944–47) and was also president of the Muslim Chamber of Commerce Delhi (1947–48).

Following the path to [[Partition of India]], Habib Rahimtoola canvassed for the Muslim League in the [[1946 Indian provincial elections|1946 elections]]. He was president of the Bombay Muslim League Parliamentary Board for Local Bodies from 1945 until 1947. Simultaneously he also remained President of the Bombay Muslim Students Union from 1946 to 1948. [[Muhammad Ali Jinnah|Jinnah]] had also nominated him to be the senior Muslim member in the Government of India's Food Delegation to the [[United Kingdom]] and [[United States]] in 1946.

By August 1947, Habib Rahimtoola was sent to receive the [[Independence of Pakistan]] formally from the [[British Government]]. He also held the honor of unfurling the [[Flag of Pakistan|Pakistan Flag]] abroad for the first time. Rahimtoola remained Ambassador of [[Pakistan]] to the United Kingdom during this period from 1947 until 1952. He was the leader of Pakistani delegations including the Inter-Allied Repatriation Agency 1948, [[1948 Commonwealth Prime Ministers' Conference|Prime Minister's Conference London 1948]], [[Freedom of the Press]] Conference 1948, International Trade and Employment Conference Geneva 1948, Commonwealth Finance Ministers Conference 1949, South East Asian Conference on [[Colombo Plan]] 1950, [[General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade|G.A.T.T.]] Conference 1951 and [[1952 Commonwealth Prime Ministers' Economic Conference|Commonwealth Finance Minister's Conference 1952]].

In 1952 Habib Rahimtoola officially formed part of the proclamation of Queen [[Elizabeth II]] to the throne of the United Kingdom. In the same year he was appointed as Ambassador to [[France]] where he stayed until the end of 1953. During his tenure, In 1953 he led the Pakistani Delegation to [[UNESCO]] in [[Paris]].

By 1953 Rahimtoola returned to Pakistan and took over as [[Governor of Sind]]. He held the post for just over a year until the end of 1954. In 1954 he was posted to [[Governor of Punjab, Pakistan|Punjab as Governor]].{{citation needed|date=October 2020}}

==Honors==

Habib Rahimtoola was Fellow of the Royal Photographic Society, Royal Society of Arts and the Royal Commonwealth Society.

He was recipient of the Melvin Jones Award from the United States.

Rahimtoola was also recipient of the First Class Order of the Sacred Treasure from the Emperor of Japan.
He founded the Photographic Society of Pakistan.

==Other political offices==

Apart from being the [[Governor of Punjab (Pakistan)|Governor of Punjab]] and [[Governor of Sindh]], he served as the [[Commerce Minister of Pakistan|Federal Minister of Commerce and Industries]] of Pakistan and chairman Pakistan Red Cross. He continued in public service until his retirement in the late 1970s.

==Business affairs==
In the late 1950s, he entered private business by setting up an investment company called Bandenawaz (Pvt) Ltd. Habib also served as Minister in various capacities of Commerce, Industries and Petroleum. He also led the Pakistan trade delegations to the [[Bandung Conference|Afro Asian Conference in Bundung]] 1955 and British East Africa 1956. After the declaration of martial law in 1958 under General [[Ayub Khan (President of Pakistan)|Ayub Khan]], Habib Rahimtoola withdrew from active politics. He was though appointed as chairman of the newly formed [[Karachi Development Authority]] in 1958 – as a post he held until 1960.
 
During the 1960s, Habib Rahimtoola ventured and focused into industrial business. He was chairman of the board of directors of several reputable firms, namely, British Oxygen Limited, Pakistan Cables Limited, [[United Bank Limited]], Brooke Bond Limited, Bandenawaz Limited, Metal Box [Pakistan] Limited, Aspro Nicholas Pakistan Limited, Chambon Pakistan Limited, Organon Pakistan Limited, and Coates Brothers Pakistan Limited.

Following the separation of East Pakistan in 1971, Habib Rahimtoola's business interests suffered a major setback. He however continued his support for Pakistan serving as Chair of the Pakistan Red Cross on the insistence of then President Yahya Khan, followed by the tenure of Zulfiqar Ali Buutto.  Rahimtoola was awarded the Pakistan Movement Gold Medal by Prime Minister Junejo in 1987.

He also served on the boards of various multinational and national companies in Pakistan as either a director or chairman, including United Bank Ltd, Eastern Federal Insurance, [[Brooke Bond]], Pakistan Oxygen (now BOC Pakistan), Aspro-Nicholas (now [[Reckitt Benckiser]]), Organon Pakistan (part of [[AkzoNobel]]) and Pakistan Cables (BICC).
<ref name="url55th Independence Day Celebrations">{{cite web |url=http://www.pakpost.gov.pk/philately/stamps2002/independence_day.html |title=55th Independence Day Celebrations |accessdate=2009-06-08}}</ref>

==Accolade==
The road connecting Shahr-e-Faisal to the National Stadium in Karachi is named 'Habib Rahimtoola Road' in lieu of his services as founding Chairman of the Karachi Development Authority <ref name="Habib Rahimtoola Road">{{cite web |url=http://wikimapia.org/5567003/Karsaz-Road-Habib-Ibrahim-Rahimtoola-Road |title=Habib Rahimtoola Road}}</ref>

In 2002 the Pakistan Post issued commemorative stamps of Habib Rahimtoola on occasion of the 55th Independence Day Celebrations <ref name="Pakistan Post issued commemorative stamps of Habib Rahimtoola">{{cite web |url=http://www.pakpost.gov.pk/philately/stamps2002/independence_day.html |title=Pakistan Post issued commemorative stamps of Habib Rahimtoola}}</ref>

==Personal life==

Habib Rahimtoola's father Sir [[Ibrahim Rahimtoola]] was a noted Indian Politician who remained Mayor of Bombay city and served as President of the Central Legislative Assembly.<ref>{{cite web|title=Habib Rahimtoola's father Sir Ibrahim Rahimtoola was a noted Indian reformer and parliamentarian who remained Mayor of Bombay city and served as President of the Central Legislative Assembly.|url=http://ismaili.net/heritage/node/20710}}</ref>

His uncle [[Jaffer Rahimtoola]] and cousin [[Hoosenally Rahimtoola]] both served as active Bombay Legislators and remained Mayors accordingly.<ref>{{cite web|title=His uncle Jafar Rahimtoola and cousin Hoosenaly Rahimtoola both served as active Bombay politicians and remained Mayors accordingly.|url=http://ismaili.net/heritage/node/20716}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=His uncle Jafar Rahimtoola and cousin Hoosenaly Rahimtoola both served as active Bombay politicians and remained Mayors accordingly.|url=http://ismaili.net/heritage/node/33421}}</ref>

His brother [[Fazal Rahimtoola]] remained an active Politician before and after partition of the Indian sub-continent.<ref>{{cite web|title=His brother Fazal Rahimtoola remained an active politician before and after partition of the sub-continentfrom India|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=53F-AAAAMAAJ&q=fazal+rahimtoola+habib|author1 = Nostradamus|year = 1986}}</ref>

Habib married Zubeida Sultan Chinoy in 1936. The couple had two sons and one daughter from their union.<ref>{{cite web|title=Habib married Zubeida Sultan Chinoy in 1936. The couple had two sons and one daughter from their union|date=19 July 2015 |url=https://tribune.com.pk/story/920121/the-queen-of-hearts-zubeida-habib-rahimtoola/}}</ref>

==Death==

Habib Rahimtoola died on 2 January 1991 whilst resident in [[Karachi]], [[Pakistan]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Habib Rahimtoola passed away on January 2, 1991 whilst resident in Karachi, Pakistan|year = 1991|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=9FZTAAAAYAAJ&q=habib+rahimtoola}}</ref> His obituary was published in the United Kingdom in connection with the relationships he had established and nurtured over a lifetime.<ref>{{cite web|title=His obituary was published in the United Kingdom in connection with the relationships he had established and nurtured over a lifetime|year = 1991|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=NHUSAQAAMAAJ&q=habib+rahimtoola}}</ref>

extract: Habib Ibrahim Rahimtoola (10 March 1912 – 2 January 1991) was a Pakistani politician, and diplomat primarily based in Karachi.
